summary: Big Knob tower in Perry County, built 1921 by the state Department of Forestry and removed in 1994; 1921 notices disagree on height (60 or 70 ft). Site not described today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1994 per the register. A 2016 state forest plan still uses the Big Knob Tower site as a location name; no source describes what remains.

staffing.status: towerman J. E. Odell from October 1921; Frank Nethkin on duty in 1936

access.note: The 2016 state forest plan describes a vista reached by a trail off Kansas Valley Road, just below the Big Knob Tower site.

events.note: Steel tower erected on Big Knob; 60 ft per the October 19 notice, 70 ft per the October 4 notice
J. E. Odell of New Germantown, named as observer in the October 19 notice, went on duty for the fall fire season on October 1
A 10-by-12-foot cabin put up at the base of the tower for the towerman
Weather Bureau equipment installed in the Big Knob Air Weather Station near Blain (notice of February 3, 1932)
Frank Nethkin the towerman; snowbound for ten days in January, supplies dropped by army airplane
Register says the tower was removed

evidence.supports: The steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and removed in 1994
evidence.quote: This steel Aermotor tower was built in 1921 and was removed in 1994.

evidence.supports: The register names the Perry County site Big Knob Tower Site
evidence.quote: Big Knob Tower Site (Perry County) | Former Fire Lookout Sites

evidence.supports: The site was registered on September 16, 2008
The Department of Forestry erected a 60-foot steel tower on Big Knob in Jackson Township, Perry County, in 1921
evidence.quote: The Department of Forestry has erected a 60-foot steel forest fire observation tower on Big Knob, between the Tuscarora and Connocochcaque mountains, in Jackson township, Perry county.

evidence.supports: The tower was one of fifty similar towers put up in three months
evidence.quote: This is one of the fifty similar towers that has been put up by the Department of Forestry during the last three months in various parts of the state.

evidence.supports: An October 4, 1921 notice gave the tower as 70 feet
evidence.quote: At Big Knob there is erected a 70-foot steel tower, from which point the eye can see practically all the land owned by the State in that territory.

evidence.supports: J. E. Odell of New Germantown manned the tower as observer
evidence.quote: The tower was constructed under the supervision of District Forester H. E. Bryner, of Blain, and it is now manned by J. E. Odell, of New Germantown, who has been engaged as a forest fire observer.

evidence.supports: Odell went on duty for the fall fire season on October 1, 1921
evidence.quote: He went on duty for the fall fire season on October 1.

evidence.supports: A 10-by-12-foot cabin was put up at the base of the tower for the towerman
evidence.quote: For the comfort and convenience of the towerman, a new cabin, 10 feet by 12 feet, has been put up at the base of the tower.

evidence.supports: Weather Bureau equipment was installed in the Big Knob Air Weather Station in February 1932, and the mountain was given as 2,200 feet
evidence.quote: All United States Weather Bureau equipment has been installed in the Big Knob Air Weather Station on Big Knob, near Blain. Big Knob is 2200 feet in height.

evidence.supports: In January 1936 Frank Nethkin was snowbound at the mountaintop cabin for ten days, and an airplane dropped groceries
evidence.quote: Groceries and provisions were dropped from an army airplane just before dusk tonight at the mountain-top cabin where Frank Nethkin, 60-year-old fire towerman, has been snow-bound for 10 days.

evidence.supports: A state fish warden was the first person Nethkin had seen in 38 days
evidence.quote: was the first human being Frank Nethkin, forest fire tower keeper in Perry County, saw in thirty-eight days.

evidence.supports: A 2016 state forest plan describes a vista reached by a trail off Kansas Valley Road just below the Big Knob Tower site
evidence.quote: The vista is accessed by a trail off of Kansas Valley Road just below the Big Knob Tower site

evidence.supports: An August 2024 post shows a small cabin at the base of the old Big Knob fire tower
evidence.quote: This small cabin sits at the base of the old Big Knob fire tower in Tuscarora State Forest.

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap labels the point Blue Knob Lookout Tower

sources.title: Big Knob (newspaper notices transcribed from 1921 to 1936)
Tuscarora State Forest 2016 Management Activity Plan
sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The October 4, 1921 notice gives 70 feet and the October 19, 1921 notice gives 60 feet. The record's 18.3 m (60 ft) follows the later notice; the register gives no height.

notes_for_editor: Record id and an OSM label say Blue Knob; every source read calls the site Big Knob in Jackson Township, Perry County. The 1921 height conflict is unresolved. Nothing read describes the site today; the 2024 Instagram post is a personal account and is the weakest source. The 2016 plan supports access but says nothing about remains. Agency taken from the 1921 notice (Department of Forestry) rather than the record's Tuscarora State Forest.
